name: 110 Herculis
description: A naked-eye star 19.2 parsecs away, 2.1 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 173667: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1 +/- 0.006 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 2.064 +/- 0.017

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 173667: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.422 +/- 0.009

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 173667: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6376 +/- 39

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 173667: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 52.06 +/- 0.24 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 19 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 2.1 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1 milliarcseconds, which gives 2.064 solar radii and 6,376 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 173667: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
